messages.message: Detector efficiency defined by a mathematical formula, given the energy x; or you can enter the coefficients for the standard equation form. Click the question mark icon for more info.
Detector efficiency defined by a mathematical formula, given the energy x; or you can enter the coefficients for the standard equation form. Click the question mark icon for more info.:

How this efficiency should be interpreted.
Intrinsic Efficiency: the probability for a x-ray or gamma striking the face of the detector, to register a full-energy detection event.
Absolute Efficiency: the probability for a x-ray or gamma from the source to register a full-energy detection event, with it being appropriate to allow scaling this efficiency by 1/r2 to other distances (i.g., is for a point-source).
Fixed Geometry - total activity: the probability for a x-ray or gamma from the source to register a full-energy detection event, and it is not appropriate to allow scaling this efficiency to other distances (e.g., for a near, or large extended source).
Fixed Geometry - activity per cm2: similar to total activity, but the efficiency curve represents efficiency per decay, per square centimeter (i.e., surface contamination).
Fixed Geometry - activity per m2: similar to per cm2, but for per square meter.
Fixed Geometry - activity per g: similar to per cm2, but for per gram of source.

Efficiency is intrinsic (per gamma striking the detector face); solid-angle corrections are applied for the source distance.
Efficiency is for one specific source/detector geometry - distances do not apply.
Efficiency uncertainties (used to propagate detector uncertainty into fit results).
Total-efficiency curve (probability of depositing any energy; input for cascade-summing corrections).
The raw per-peak efficiency measurements this DRF was made from (kept for provenance, and to anchor a Monte-Carlo characterization).
Full Monte-Carlo-parameterized response ({1} profile; valid {2}-{3} keV): off-axis and near-field efficiencies with honest uncertainties.
No Monte-Carlo parameterization - efficiencies are on-axis far-field only. Use "Characterize by MC..." to add one.

Efficiency-transfer response (an anchored efficiency curve carried to other distances/angles through the exact ray-traced detector geometry; valid {1}-{2} keV). Best accuracy on-axis at distances beyond {3}; closer or well off-axis queries are flagged and carry an honestly inflated uncertainty. For the best near-field / off-axis accuracy run a Full MC characterization ("Modify...", Geometry & MC tab).

Whether the Monte-Carlo response has been anchored to measured efficiencies (k(E) correction with covariance). "(curve)" means it was anchored to a fitted curve rather than raw measured points - slightly lower quality.
